Basically how pollux works is - 
1. his first card played every turn is strengthened
2. That same effect is applied after using his Ultimate
3. His ultimate creates a card called "sacred heart", which deals damage and bleed and can be played 3 times before exhausting
4. when you play his rouse (or sacred heart), he gets a buff that makes all his damage deal a certain % part in bleed as well, depending on how many stacks of the buff he has. Every card with "retain" in your hand *increases* the amount of stacks you get at turn end by 1. 

In conclusion on how to use that team:

Play his rouse, keep your retain cards in hand until you have a few stacks (early on you can ignore this since him and saya will just ruin anything anyways), when you have sacred heart, his ult *and* saya's 0 cost card all available, use his sacred heart, then saya 0 cost, then use his ult, then use the sacred heart he generated and the one you will have pulled from saya's 0 cost again (it gets put on the top of the draw pile after being played), and then use his other damaging cards. If you have his cleansing judgement, that thing will do pretty great damage for relatively cheap. Only play his 2 cost *after* having played both your sacred hearts, because it will pull 2 cards with the lowest cost. Oh you can also use it to guarantee you pulling Saya's 0 cost if you have the rest of the puzzle assembled
importantly, in this comp you don't want to use saya 0 cost to cycle through your deck, because it has retain, so you're better off keeping it in hand until you can actually use it with effect

once you have e3 pollux (if you want that... which you kinda do, since it's a pretty big buff), there's one more thing to take into consideration, namely that after you play your sacred heart for the third time, the next card he plays will *also* get the buff his first card and the first card after ultimate gets, so it might be smart to play every sacred heart once after you get it, so your burst turn gets stronger
